name: discovery-sbml-recovery
title: Discovery-engine SBML recovery — can the cycle build faithful flat SBML models from data?
lead:
A methods investigation. Each study hides a known ground-truth SBML behind its
synthetic trajectories and asks the discovery-engine cycle to rebuild a flat
SBML that matches — graded on trajectory fidelity, structural/parameter
recovery against the oracle, and parsimony. As the loop runs, every capability
gap it hits is logged in a capability ledger and built as a modular
process-bigraph process, so the investigation's second deliverable is a growing
vivarium-style toolkit, not just a verdict.

at_a_glance.role: Baseline — calibrate recovery on linear/bilinear mass-action; establishes trajectory + structural scoring.
Elementary vs reduced rate law — can the loop recover Michaelis-Menten, and which form is parsimonious?
Nonlinearity/bistability — frontier-driven refinement where the data underdetermine the mechanism.
Dynamic structure — recover a limit-cycle topology, the hardest structural recovery.
Adversarial — a stochastic system with no flat-SBML form; passes by being correctly REJECTED.

biological_story:
The four scenarios form a difficulty ladder, each stressing a different part of
the build -> compare -> refine loop.

Mass-action (A -> B, reversible binding A + B <-> C) is the floor: linear /
bilinear rates, a handful of reactions. If the cycle can't recover this, nothing
downstream matters — so it calibrates the trajectory and structural scoring.

Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics forces a modelling choice: recover the
elementary mechanism (E + S <-> ES -> E + P) or the reduced saturating rate law.
Both fit the data; parsimony and structural scoring decide which counts as
"recovered", and the loop must be able to propose a non-elementary rate law.

A Hill-function gene switch adds genuine nonlinearity and bistability — the data
alone underdetermine the mechanism, so the cycle's frontier (what the current
candidate fails to explain) has to drive the search, not a one-shot fit.

An oscillator (repressilator / Brusselator) is dynamic structure: a limit cycle
the recovered topology must reproduce qualitatively, not just point-wise. This is
where we expect structural recovery to be hardest and where the capability gaps
(reaction proposal, rate-law fitting) bite most.
question:
Run as a closed build -> simulate -> compare -> refine loop, can the
discovery-engine cycle recover faithful FLAT SBML models from synthetic
time-series targets across a ladder of biological scenarios (mass-action ->
enzyme kinetics -> gene switch -> oscillator), and what modular, vivarium-style
capabilities must be built to close the gaps where it can't?
hypothesis:
The cycle recovers flat SBML to within trajectory tolerance AND
structural/parameter match for mass-action and Michaelis-Menten out of the box;
nonlinearity (Hill switch) and dynamic structure (oscillator) expose specific
missing capabilities (candidate-reaction proposal, rate-law fitting, structural
scoring, non-recoverability detection), each of which, once built as a modular
process, extends the recoverable frontier. Parsimony separates genuine recovery
from overfitting.

executive.what_is_this:
A recovery benchmark: synthetic data from known SBML models across four
biological scenarios, with the discovery-engine cycle driving a closed
build -> simulate -> compare -> refine loop to rebuild flat SBML — plus a
capability ledger that turns each gap into a modular vivarium process.
executive.verdict:
Complete — all four recovery rungs and the adversarial control pass. The
discovery-engine cycle, through the register_evaluators + build_hook seams,
drives a closed generate -> run -> compare -> score -> refine loop that recovers
faithful flat SBML across the ladder: mass-action, enzyme kinetics, and the
nonlinear Hill gene switch via trajectory/gradient fitting; the Brusselator
oscillator via gradient (derivative) matching where trajectory least-squares is
ill-conditioned; and structure from scratch via SINDy sparse identification. The
adversarial stochastic (low-copy) system is correctly REJECTED as not recoverable
as a flat SBML. All seven ledger capabilities are built, and the capability-gap
bridge is prototyped so the cycle can surface and route future gaps.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The discovery-engine cycle, given a synthetic oracle, can build faithful flat
SBML for simple kinetics, and the cases where it fails are exactly the ones
that tell us which modular capabilities to build next.
evidence_for: Mass-action, enzyme (Michaelis-Menten), and the nonlinear Hill gene switch recover to ~1e-9 trajectory error with exact parameters from a 2x-wrong start.
The Brusselator oscillator recovers (A=1, B=3) via gradient (derivative) matching, where raw-trajectory least-squares fails (ill-conditioned on a limit cycle).
SINDy sparse identification recovers the mass-action reaction network (A->B, A+B<->C) from trajectories alone, no prior structure.
The adversarial stochastic low-copy trajectory is correctly flagged non-recoverable (polynomial-RHS R^2 ~0.05), so the method rejects systems with no flat-SBML form.
caveats: Synthetic targets are an oracle, not biology — success means the method recovered a KNOWN model, not that it discovered real mechanism.
Flat SBML only — hierarchical/submodel composition is out of scope here (that is the sibling sbml-decomposition investigation).
Recovery is scored against ground truth; without the oracle (real data) the same loop has no structural answer key, only trajectory fit.

competing_frameworks.name: fit-is-enough
competing_frameworks.prediction: matching the target trajectory is sufficient to call a model recovered
competing_frameworks.discriminated_by: structural-recovery + parsimony scoring — a curve-fit that matches the data but invents the wrong reactions fails the structural and parsimony gates

competing_frameworks.name: everything-is-recoverable-flat-SBML
competing_frameworks.prediction: any dynamics, given the right data, can be captured as a flat SBML reaction network
competing_frameworks.discriminated_by: the planned adversarial scenario — a system whose faithful form is not a flat reaction network (non-recoverability detector should flag it)

competing_frameworks.name: no-engine-needed
competing_frameworks.prediction: you don't need the discovery cycle; a one-shot global fitter recovers the model
competing_frameworks.discriminated_by: recover-gene-switch + recover-oscillator, where iterative frontier-driven refinement is what closes the structural gap a one-shot fit misses

studies.name: recover-mass-action
studies.title: Recover mass-action kinetics
studies.question:
Given only synthetic time-series generated from a known mass-action SBML model
(A -> B, reversible binding A + B <-> C), can the discovery-engine cycle rebuild
a flat SBML that reproduces the trajectories and recovers the actual reactions
and rate constants?
methods: one tellurium process over the candidate flat-SBML model

studies.name: recover-enzyme-kinetics
studies.title: Recover enzyme kinetics (Michaelis-Menten)
studies.question:
From synthetic data generated by a known enzyme-kinetics model, can the cycle
recover a flat SBML — and does it recover the elementary mechanism
(E + S <-> ES -> E + P) or the reduced Michaelis-Menten rate law, and which is
the parsimonious answer the data actually support?
methods: one tellurium process over the candidate flat-SBML model

studies.name: recover-gene-switch
studies.title: Recover a Hill gene switch
studies.question:
From synthetic data of a bistable Hill-repression gene switch, can the cycle
recover a flat SBML that reproduces both stable branches and the nonlinear
(Hill) regulation — a case where the data alone underdetermine the mechanism?
methods: one tellurium process over the candidate flat-SBML model

studies.name: recover-oscillator
studies.title: Recover an oscillator
studies.question:
From synthetic data of a limit-cycle oscillator (repressilator or Brusselator),
can the cycle recover a flat SBML whose topology reproduces the oscillation —
period and amplitude — as sustained dynamics, not just a point-wise fit over one
window?
methods: one tellurium process over the candidate flat-SBML model

studies.name: recover-stochastic-abm
studies.title: Reject a stochastic system (no flat-SBML form)
studies.question:
Does the recovery pipeline correctly REFUSE to recover a flat SBML from a single
low-copy stochastic trajectory — recognizing the ABM/stochastic boundary where no
deterministic flat-SBML reaction network faithfully fits the data?
methods: one tellurium process over the candidate flat-SBML model
